VibePascal v55 Win64 compiler -- a missing -FU/-FE output directory is created,
not complained about
Source commit: eae5d3e919a26a7db19937da10da1c8b610b17da
Compiler fix:  4d10b26fe7  (compiler/options.pas)
Parent release: v54 (b7d2d9676ecf1d7d8250cd460b9c48069920513e)
Built: 2026-09-10, cross-compiled Linux x86_64 -> Win64 (-Apecoff -Xi) from the
       self-hosted Linux compiler 19f526bd6be0ec63fca96c4d1b77e19d
ppcx64.exe md5:    30D80F9225B7356869BB2639797D1045
ppcx64.exe sha256: 4B9BA08C12612D6C0679445332F74153686E53831D9D0E60F9017C3A662F5C8B

WHAT WAS BROKEN
---------------
Unpacking this tarball and compiling anything in a fresh directory failed on
the FIRST build, before you had written a line of your own code:

    hello.pas(4,1) Error: Can't create object file: .\units\x86_64-win64\hello.o (error code: 3)
    hello.pas(4,1) Fatal: Can't create object .\units\x86_64-win64\hello.o
    Fatal: Compilation aborted

Nothing you did caused it. bin/fpc.cfg carries "-FU./units/$FPCTARGET", the
compiler had never created that directory, and the diagnostic named a FILE
rather than the directory -- so the cure (mkdir units\x86_64-win64) was not
discoverable from the message. Anyone who unpacked v54 or earlier and typed
one compile command hit this. Everyone installing through auto-update.bat was
immune, because that path passes -n and suppresses this config entirely.

Extracting the units tarball did NOT help, and it is worth saying why: the two
kinds of path in fpc.cfg are anchored differently.

    -Fu$FPCBINDIR/../units/$FPCTARGET   SEARCH  -- relative to the COMPILER
    -FU./units/$FPCTARGET               OUTPUT  -- relative to YOUR directory

Search resolves into the install tree; output resolves wherever you happen to
be standing. BuildMaster measured this on the published v54 bytes with all
1803 v52 PPUs present in the install tree and it still failed identically. No
tarball and no installer mkdir can satisfy an output path that follows the
user around, which is why this had to be fixed in the compiler.

WHAT CHANGED
------------
-FE (exe/link output) and -FU (unit/object output) name where the COMPILER
writes, not where you already put something, so a missing one is a chore for
the compiler rather than an error to hand back. Both are now created up front,
recursively.

The existing "Path ... does not exist" error is still reported -- but only
after creation has actually been TRIED and FAILED. So a genuinely impossible
path (a component that is a plain file, a read-only parent, a bad drive) still
stops the build, with the same message, and now it arrives during option
processing and names the DIRECTORY instead of surfacing later as a codegen
"error code: 3" on a file.

One behaviour change to be aware of: -FE on a missing directory used to be an
error and now creates the directory. -FU never had that diagnostic at all.

bin/fpc.cfg is UNCHANGED in substance -- "-FU./units/$FPCTARGET" is still
there, deliberately. It now does what it always meant: your .o/.ppu land in
./units/x86_64-win64 and that directory appears if it is missing. Deleting the
line would also have made compiles work, but it would have scattered .o/.ppu
next to your sources instead, which is a worse default and a change nobody
asked for. (The comment block in that file was rewritten to drop a stale
"v32-rc" version literal; ask the compiler with `ppcx64 -iV` instead.)

Distribution requirements:
- COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY refresh on top of v54. Only compiler/options.pas
  changed. No PPU format change, no RTL change, no package change.
- Pair with vibepascal-v52-win64-units.tar.gz (the v52 1803-PPU unit set,
  still current -- v53, v54 and v55 are all binary-only refreshes on it).
  Existing v52/v53/v54 unit installs stay valid and do NOT need re-pulling.
- Install through C:\Lazarus\auto-update.bat.

VALIDATION
----------
Linux, on isolated A/B compilers built from the same tree (the production
ppcx64 and its units were never touched by these runs):
- 11-corner -FU/-FE matrix: -FU relative one level missing, -FU relative three
  levels missing, -FU absolute missing, -FE missing, -FU and -FE missing
  together, -FU on an existing directory, no -FU/-FE at all, -FU under a plain
  FILE, -FU under a read-only parent, a UNIT compile writing both .ppu and .o
  into a missing -FU, and the shipped "-FU./units/$FPCTARGET" config-file
  shape read through @cfg. Baseline 4/11 -> fixed 11/11. Every corner that is
  supposed to succeed had its produced binary RUN, not merely linked; the two
  corners that must still refuse still exit non-zero with no internal error.
- Full corpus tests/test t*.pp, 1981 tests, compile status + run exit code
  compared between baseline and fixed compilers: 1981 SAME, 0 DIFF.
- Pre-fix control: the SHIPPED v54 Linux compiler (eb57aa4d) was re-run
  through the same matrix this cycle and still fails 7 of 11, so the matrix
  can fail and the comparison means something.
- Self-host fixpoint: stage3 == stage4 byte-identical
  (19f526bd6be0ec63fca96c4d1b77e19d). The stage2->stage3 delta was exactly two
  bytes -- the producing compiler's own embedded build-date stamp, 2026/09/03
  carried in by an incremental stage1 versus 2026/09/10 from the first clean
  build -- not a codegen difference.
- vp_win64_smoke RESULT: PASS and tinlinevarnativeint1 checks=45 fails=0 under
  -Munleashed on the self-hosted Linux compiler.

Win64, running THESE bytes under wine64 (see dist/win64-runtime-proof.sh):
- Fresh directory, shipped bin/fpc.cfg, NO mkdir: exit 0, the compiler created
  units\x86_64-win64\hello.o, produced hello.exe, and hello.exe RAN.
- Negative control, same directory shape, the preserved pre-fix v54 exe
  (293f3c98a26ff3233d88550259ba8b1f): exit 1 with exactly the two error lines
  quoted at the top of this file, and no output produced. The A/B is on the
  real PE bytes, not a rebuild.
- No semantic drift: tinlinevarnativeint1 reports "checks=45 fails=0
  NativeInt=8" under BOTH -Munleashed and -Mdelphiunicode, and
  tests/test/vp_win64_smoke.pp exits 0 with RESULT: PASS.

LIMIT, stated plainly: wine is NOT Windows. It runs the real shipped PE bytes
and real x86-64 instructions on an independent reimplementation of the Win64
API, so codegen, PE layout and RTL-startup defects do surface -- but nobody
has yet run this compiler on genuine Windows hardware. That ask is still open.
